name: Protected-priority two-band representation transition
classification: One terminal representation experiment, not observed terrain, error correction, hydrological DEM or production adoption
basis: Unencoded retained Swiss z14 sum/count basis aggregated to z12; decoded common z13 aggregated to z12 under the same Mercator-area mean. Strict complete-cell support and bilinear pixel-centre prolongation, as in terrain-scale diagnostic. S_z at z12-14 comes from complete retained regional-parent cells (coarse delivery need not be limited to the old complete-tile inventory); at z15-18 use existing fine Swiss tiles. Existing fine Swiss delivery is immutable; C_z is existing common delivery or declared z13 overzoom.
heightPolicy: Preserve both native source heights: Swiss LN02, common EGM2008. A scalar transition has heterogeneous height semantics, not a common physical vertical CRS. No transformation or fitted shift. Valid only as explicitly synthetic visual-representation diagnostic; never an analytical elevation or accurate fused DEM. Physical common-frame adoption remains unresolved.
weightRule: q(t)=1-10t^3+15t^4-6t^5, t clamped to [0,1]. b=q((r-1500)/2500); d=q((r-3000)/1000). These are declared geometric representation controls, not uncertainty or a fitted source-error model.
formula: For each z>=12, T_z = Cb_z + b*(Sb_z-Cb_z) + d*(S_z-Sb_z) + (1-d)*(C_z-Cb_z). Endpoint branches copy pure S_z when r<=1500 and pure C_z when r>=4000, avoiding cancellation/encoding drift. Sb/Cb are prolonged z12 broad controls. No correction fit, smoothing of source products or per-sector weight tuning.
coarseParents: Create only diagnostic z11 and z10 of the resulting z12 field using sum/count area means on the unchanged common context with regional-derived influence recorded. Do not directly swap to common below z12. Any remaining handoff below z10 is retained and reported, not solved by generating to z0. Coarse aggregation is not modification of underlying fine protected heights.
supportPolicy: Only complete retained regional cells at z12-14 and existing complete fine delivery tiles at z15-18 can supply S_z or Sb. Coarse partial tiles can be constructed only when every cell has explicit legitimate Swiss or common support; Swiss partial-cell means are never full heights. Before generation verify full annulus and interpolation halos at all requested levels; if the exact existing products do not support it, stop with input/delivery-support failure. Do not acquire, extrapolate, pad missing Swiss or silently shrink/shift the collar. Outer circle is an engineering evaluation footprint, not a scientific seamline.
glacierPolicy: Retain SGI1973/2016/2023 masks and unknown per-cell epoch. Source priority preserves Swiss in pure interior, including ice. Transition may cross change terrain but is labelled synthetic multi-epoch; no glacier residual is fitted as error, no blended height is represented as an observation date or change estimate. Report ice and non-ice separately.
provenance: Pure common, pure regional, same-family generalisation, and derived transition/derived parents distinguished. Retain signed band operations, b/d fields, source references/versions, support fractions and change masks. b and d alone are not simple source contribution/confidence weights; with b != d some filter coefficients can be negative. Retain complete processing operator for reconstruction.
controls: pure Swiss regional family inside complete support

cameras.edgePositions: LV95 centre plus r=3000,3500,4000,4250m at eight azimuths, all around the designed circular footprint; retain original west/south support cameras as controls.
cameras.navigation: One centre approach/outward zoom sequence; separate west and south lateral sequences from interior through collar to common and back, including warm and cold parent loading. Record requested and actually used mesh/relief DEM levels, not camera zoom alone.
cameras.satellite: Existing satellite mode at centre/west/south close checks to isolate geometry; no imagery change

numericalMetrics: 705 protected fine samples plus every eligible protected cell compared to immutable source level
component closure and signed contributor reconstruction
cross-boundary intercept and gradient profiles at eight azimuths plus dense worst-section search
induced gradient term (Sb-Cb)*grad(b)+(Rs-Rc)*grad(d), separately from source terrain slopes
height and detail retention by radius, level, stable/steep/change class
new extrema and drainage-direction/curvature changes, no hydrological truth claim
same-coordinate parent/child RMS/p95/max and broad correction area/amount
support, tile-edge and deterministic output hashes
failureCriteria: any protected fine change beyond one Terrarium quantisation step (1/256m); pure branches should be byte-exact
any outside-common change beyond one quantisation step
missing valid transition support or fabricated Swiss data
introduced cross-boundary height intercept greater than 0.1m after accounting for genuine local slope
induced gradient magnitude p95 greater than 0.05 m/m, or any connected segment >=100m above 0.10 m/m
new synthetic ridge/depression/channel identifiable in profiles and captures
persistent wall, crack, strong relief band, severe source-switch pop or lost protected regional structure in any required sequence/rotation
unknown contributor/operator or relabelled height/epoch semantics
criteriaMeaning: Gradient/intercept limits are predeclared engineering rejection guards, not surveyed accuracy or universal Atlas tolerances. Passing them does not override visual failure or prove geomorphological correctness. Report all collar deformation, including tens of metres, and preserved detail; smoothness alone cannot pass.
successCriteria: All preservation/support/provenance and numerical guards pass; meaningful Swiss detail remains in protected close views; progressive residual attenuation occurs in the declared collar; no unacceptable geometry/relief/navigation artifact across all required views. Coarse regime may use same-family summaries where visually equivalent; no claim of common-source identity there. Remaining finite-context/coarse-handoff limits documented.
terminalRule: One geometry, one two-band rule, one broad level. No blend-width search, extra acquisitions or alternate algorithm. At most repair one narrow implementation defect without changing the method. Then freeze the Terrain Hierarchy Contract with demonstrated behaviour and failures explicit, regardless of result; generic implementation and second-region validation are separate tasks.
